newsitem.title: UK: London gold edges down on fresh fears of IMF sales.
newsitem.headline: London gold edges down on fresh fears of IMF sales.

text.p: Gold prices crept down on Friday morning on a fresh report about possible gold sales by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), but little substantial movement was expected ahead of a three-day U.S. weekend.
"There was some Far East and Swiss selling this morning, but then it bounced a bit on dealer short-covering," a dealer said.
Bullion fixed at $387.25 per ounce, 75 cents down from Thursday afternoon and compared with a London close of $388.25.
The New York Times said on Friday the IMF had sent a new plan to member governments this week on selling some of its $40 billion in bullion holdings to finance debt reduction for poor countries.
IMF member countries have long been wrangling over such a plan and failed in June at the Group of Seven countries meeting in Lyon, France to agree on a proposal to sell five percent of its stocks.
The G-7 countries -- the United States, Japan, Germany, Britain, France, Italy and Canada -- postponed any decision until the autumn.
Bullion dealers said there did not appear to be anything substantially new in the newspaper report, but it affected sentiment since it reminded the market that sales may be drawing near.
"Prices moved because this time maybe people think it's really going to happen and also the market's been so quiet," a dealer said.

Dealers and analysts were mixed on whether gold would resume its medium-term uptrend next week, with some expecting a challenge of $390 resistance soon, and others seeing a move down to recent lows around $385.50.
The white metals inched down in sympathy with gold, with silver losing a few cents to $5.20 per ounce.
Some analysts saw silver as the key to the precious complex, with a breakout from its current range of $5.16-$5.25 determining the direction of the others.
Dealers were watching the fallout from a Financial Times report that Russia had closed its agency which oversees precious metals sales.
There were concerns that the Kremlin would find it easier to liquidate stocks to cover budget shortfalls, it added.
Platinum eased to a low of $396 an ounce in New York on Thursday night, interrupting an uptrend that started in early July.
It was quoted at midday on Friday at $397.50, down $1.80 from the London close, while palladium was unchanged at $126.00 per ounce.
